registry.description: Craving is the most acute form of desire — the pressing, urgent want that will not wait and has difficulty being satisfied. The Greek vocabulary here covers both the sick longing of intense desire and the aspiration toward something felt as necessary. Craving is desire at the level of physical urgency: the body (or the person considered bodily) pressing toward what it needs or has been trained to want. Scripture is not contemptuous of craving in itself, but it consistently asks whether the craving is rightly directed.
